games.title: Fraction Fusion
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to add and subtract fractions with different denominators and mixed numbers, using the concept of equivalent fractions
games.instruction: Make the denominators the same, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Find a common denominator before you add or subtract.

games.title: Fraction Factory
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to multiply simple pairs of proper fractions, writing the answer in its simplest form [for example, 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8]; divide proper fractions by whole numbers [for example, 1/3 ÷ 2 = 1/6]
games.instruction: Work out the fraction in its simplest form, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify.

games.title: Percent Power
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to solve problems involving the calculation of percentages [for example, of measures, and such as 15% of 360] and the use of percentages for comparison
games.instruction: Work out the percentage, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Find 10% or 1% first, then build up to the percentage you need.

questions.ask: What is 15% of 360?
What is 10% of 80?
What is 25% of 60?
What is 50% of 140?
What is 75% of 200?
What is 5% of 40?
What is 30% of £70?
What is 1% of 600?
What is 60% of 25?
Which amount is the largest?

games.title: Formula Fixers
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use simple formulae; express missing number problems algebraically; find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns; enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables
games.instruction: Use the formula or find the missing number, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Put the numbers into the formula one step at a time, then check.

questions.ask: n + 7 = 15. What is n?
4y = 28. What is y?
30 − m = 12. What is m?
If a = 5, what is 3a + 2?
6 + k = 2k. What is k?
Perimeter of a square: P = 4s. If s = 6 cm, what is P?
Taxi cost = £2 + £3 per mile. What does a 4 mile ride cost?
a + b = 10. Which pair works?
2x + y = 12. Which pair works?
a + b = 5 and a, b are whole numbers from 1 to 4. How many pairs (a, b)?

games.title: Miles And Metres
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use, read, write and convert between standard units, converting measurements of length, mass, volume and time from a smaller unit of measure to a larger unit, and vice versa, using decimal notation to up to 3 decimal places; convert between miles and kilometres
games.instruction: Convert the measure, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Remember 5 miles is about 8 km, and check which way you multiply.

questions.ask: 5 miles is about how many kilometres?
About how many miles is 40 km?
About how many kilometres is 15 miles?
What is 3.075 kg in grams?
What is 2,450 ml in litres?
What is 0.125 km in metres?
What is 375 cm in metres?
What is 150 minutes in hours?
What is 4.2 m in millimetres?
What is 9 g in kilograms?

games.title: Mean Machine
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to calculate and interpret the mean as an average
games.instruction: Find the mean, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.

questions.ask: What is the mean of 4, 6 and 8?
What is the mean of 3, 5, 7 and 9?
What is the mean of 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50?
What is the mean of 2, 2 and 5?
What is the mean of 0, 0 and 9?
What is the mean of 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5?
Temperatures were 5°C, 9°C, 7°C and 11°C. What is the mean?
Books read: Monday 12, Tuesday 8, Wednesday 10. What is the mean per day?
The mean of 3 numbers is 7. What is their total?
The mean of 4 numbers is 5. Three are 2, 4 and 6. What is the fourth?

games.title: Angle Sleuths
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise angles where they meet at a point, are on a straight line, or are vertically opposite, and find missing angles; find unknown angles in any triangles, quadrilaterals, and regular polygons
games.instruction: Find the missing angle, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Triangles total 180°, quadrilaterals total 360°, and a straight line is 180°.

questions.ask: A triangle has angles 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
A right-angled triangle has a 35° angle. What is the other angle?
An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40°. What is each base angle?
What is each angle in an equilateral triangle?
A quadrilateral has angles 90°, 90° and 110°. What is the fourth?
A quadrilateral has angles 100°, 80° and 75°. What is the fourth?
Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
Two lines cross. One angle is 130°. What is the angle next to it?
Angles on a straight line are 47° and ?
What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?

games.title: Big Times Rocket
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to multiply multi-digit numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit whole number using the formal written method of long multiplication
games.instruction: Use long multiplication, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Remember the zero placeholder when you multiply by the tens digit.

games.title: Division Den
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit whole number using the formal written method of long division, and interpret remainders as whole number remainders, fractions, or by rounding, as appropriate for the context; divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit number using the formal written method of short division where appropriate, interpreting remainders according to the context
games.instruction: Use a written method, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Check how many times the divisor fits at each step, then try again.

questions.ask: Write 432 ÷ 15 as a mixed number.
75 pizzas are shared equally between 12 tables. How much does each table get?
500 children go on a trip. Each coach holds 45. How many coaches are needed?

games.title: Ten Million Ranker
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to read, write, order and compare numbers up to 10 000 000 and determine the value of each digit; round any whole number to a required degree of accuracy
games.instruction: Compare the numbers or round them, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Start with the millions and work along, digit by digit.

questions.ask: Which number is the largest?
Which number is the smallest?
Round 3,682,415 to the nearest million.
Round 3,682,415 to the nearest 100,000.
Round 5,349,999 to the nearest 10,000.
Round 9,999,600 to the nearest 1000.
What is the value of the 6 in 2,604,513?
Which number is between 6,500,000 and 6,600,000?
Which of these is ten million?

games.title: Common Factor Quest
games.skillName: Common factors, common multiples and primes
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify common factors, common multiples and prime numbers
games.instruction: Think about factors and multiples, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. List the factors or multiples of each number, then look for a match.

questions.ask: What is the highest common factor of 18 and 30?
What is the highest common factor of 24 and 40?
Which number is a common factor of 21 and 35, other than 1?
Which number is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
What is the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8?
What is the lowest common multiple of 5 and 7?
Which number is prime?
Which number is NOT prime?
How many prime numbers are between 20 and 30?
What are the prime factors of 12?

games.title: Simplify Squad
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use common factors to simplify fractions; use common multiples to express fractions in the same denomination; compare and order fractions, including fractions > 1
games.instruction: Simplify or compare the fractions, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Divide the top and bottom by the same number, or give them a common denominator.

questions.ask: Simplify 6/8.
Simplify 10/15.
Simplify 18/24.
Simplify 20/45.
Simplify 14/49.
Simplify 25/100.
Which fraction is equal to 2/3?
Which fraction is the largest?
Which is the smallest?
Which fraction is greater than 2?

games.title: Area Workshop
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to calculate the area of parallelograms and triangles; recognise that shapes with the same areas can have different perimeters and vice versa; recognise when it is possible to use formulae for area and volume of shapes
games.instruction: Work out the area, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. A triangle is half of base × height; a parallelogram is base × height.

questions.ask: A triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. What is its area?
A triangle has base 10 cm and height 7 cm. What is its area?
A triangle has base 6 cm and height 9 cm. What is its area?
A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 4 cm. What is its area?
A parallelogram has base 12 cm, height 6 cm, slant side 7 cm. Area?
A triangle has area 30 cm² and base 10 cm. What is its height?
A parallelogram has area 48 cm² and base 8 cm. What is its height?
A 6 cm × 4 cm and an 8 cm × 3 cm rectangle have the same what?
Which rectangle has area 24 cm² and perimeter 28 cm?
Which rectangle has the same area as a 4 cm × 4 cm square?

games.title: Circle Secrets
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter and circumference and know that the diameter is twice the radius
games.instruction: Think about the parts of a circle, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. The diameter goes right across through the centre; the radius is half of it.

questions.ask: What is the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge?
What is the distance all the way round a circle called?
What is a straight line across a circle through its centre?
What is the point in the exact middle of a circle?
The diameter is how many times the radius?
A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its diameter?
A circle has a diameter of 18 cm. What is its radius?
A circle has a radius of 3.5 cm. What is its diameter?
A wheel has a diameter of 1 m. What is its radius?
